newsitem.title: USA: USX-Marathon pulls out of Ukraine.
newsitem.headline: USX-Marathon pulls out of Ukraine.

text.p: Marathon Oil Co said on Thursday it had pulled out of the Ukraine where it had been looking at the possibility of exploring for natural gas.

Company spokesman Bill Ryder told Reuters that Marathon, a unit of USX-Marathon Group, chose to withdraw after a year of preliminary work because there were still too many unanswered questions about such issues as licensing, gas marketing, security of investment, and tax and legal stability.
"They're moving slowly," Ryder said of the Ukrainian government. "They're having problems getting enabling laws to get things to work."
Ryder said Marathon had been in talks with the Ukrainian government and had done a lot of exploratory work to evaluate fields, but had gone no further. "There was no hardware over there," he said.
The company reportedly had been mulling investments up to $200 million in the Poltava natural gas field.
Ryder said Marathon had informed the government of its decision in a Jan. 6 letter.
Ryder said Marathon was intrigued by the gas prospects in the Ukraine and would be interested in going back in "if the issues we're concerned with are resolved."
But, for now, he said, Marathon's plans in the Ukraine were at an end. "There's no next step right now," Ryder said.
